78.translation: And further: for one who has supreme devotion to God, and as to God so to the teacher, to that great soul these meanings that have been taught shine forth. At the end of the body, the Lord expounds the liberating Supreme Brahman. He is attained by the one whom He Himself chooses. Śruti, Smṛti, and Purāṇa statements such as these become coherent when this is so. Therefore it is established that devotion alone is the cause of liberation.
word_for_word: for one who has supreme devotion to God
and as to God, so to the teacher
tasya ete kathitā hi arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanām
to that great soul these meanings that have been taught shine forth
deha-ante devaḥ paraṃ brahma tārakaṃ vyācaṣṭe
at the end of the body, the Lord expounds the liberating Supreme Brahman
yam eva eṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ
He is attained by the one whom He Himself chooses
Śruti, Smṛti, and Purāṇa statements such as these
become coherent when this is so
tasmāt bhaktiḥ eva mokṣa-hetuḥ iti siddham
therefore it is established that devotion alone is the cause of liberation
